topic: VSEPR Theory and Shapes of Molecules
title: VSEPR Shapes of Molecules Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
Four balloons tied at one knot never lie flat. Water is bent, carbon dioxide is straight. One simple rule decides all three: electron pairs push each other as far apart as they can. In this animated lesson for PUC and Class 11 Chemistry (NCERT Chapter 4, Chemical Bonding and Molecular Structure) we learn VSEPR theory and predict the shape of a molecule just by counting.

On the molecule bench, electron pairs spread around a central atom: linear 180°, trigonal planar 120°, tetrahedral 109.5°, trigonal bipyramidal 120° and 90°, octahedral 90°, drawn in 2D with wedges and dashes. Then lone pairs squeeze the angle from methane (109.5°) to ammonia (107°) to water (104.5°). We build the pushing order link by link, work out the see-saw shape of SF4 step by step, and meet bent, T-shaped, square pyramid and square planar shapes. Then the exam trap, an original NEET pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

This is Episode 46 of our PUC Chemistry series.

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students. For NCERT, CBSE, ICSE/ISC, PUC, NEET and JEE students.
